text:
Florian Xhekaj, Arber's younger brother, is getting his chance because of injuries. A fourth-round pick in 2023 who scored 24 goals for AHL Laval in 2024-25, he drew in for Chris Kreider and has taken Kreider's spot beside Jake Evans and Josh Anderson, though Anderson has now been hurt too.

He's played eight games with a goal and two assists, in under eight minutes a night, and the early numbers are good. Montreal takes 62% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, almost 12 points better than without him, and 56% of the shot attempts. His finishing is right on expected. He has 21 hits in eight games, which is very much the family style.

The sample is small, and our talent range is wide because of it, somewhere between 13 and 30 points over a full season. TSN wrote that he drew in as the Habs try to get back to their best hockey, and Karine Hains of The Hockey News called it a great opportunity. With Kreider out until January, he'll have time to show whether the chance numbers hold.
